newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: TENNIS-BECKER SAYS VICTORY BORDERS ON MIRACLE.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-BECKER SAYS VICTORY BORDERS ON MIRACLE.

text.p: Boris Becker said after beating Jan Siemerink in the final of $800,000 CA Trophy on Sunday that winning his first title since injuring his wrist at Wimbledon bordered on a miracle.

A weary Becker, still far from his best form, won 6-4 6-7 6-2 6-3 on the indoor hardcourt of Vienna's Stadthalle for his third title of the year after the Australian Open and the London grass-court championship at Queen's Club.
Victory came as a relief for Becker, who took a long break after rupturing a tendon in his right wrist in a third-round match at Wimbledon.
He returned to the circuit last month but recurring wrist troubles saw him pull out in the first round in Bucharest, lose in the second round in Basle and withdraw from a tournament in Lyon.
"For me this victory is like a wonder. I still don't fully understand how I did it. It is of great importance for me," Becker, visibly moved, said.
"I was never injured for such a long time and never on the wrist. I was never really sure if I would be 100 percent again.
"I spent the last four months worrying about my injury. Now I want to enjoy this victory and have fun playing tennis."
World number seven Becker will be aiming for the 48th title of his career at this week's Czech Indoor Open in Ostrava where his first round opponent is Denmark's Frederik Fetterlein.
Becker made a good start against Siemerink on Sunday, planting a forehand on the line to convert his second break chance for a quick lead in the opening game.
The Dutch left-hander failed to capitalise on four break points in the following game and Becker went on to clinch the set.
The match lost momentum in the second set when games went with serves into a tie-break. Both players missed a set point before Siemerink profited from a backhand from Becker which went wide for 9-7.
The German had difficulty holding his serve in the opening game of the third set but stepped up a gear to gain a break and edge ahead 3-1 with a thundering backhand return.
Siemerink again dropped serve and Becker clinched the set with a low forehand return.
Becker needed a single break in the fourth set to go 5-3 up and served for victory at the end of a match lasting two hours 38 minutes.
